methods: Each trial uses a fresh Play and restores saved initial body/player positions, polarities and zero velocities before the trial, compensating for automatic tool transition steps. Physical parameters, dynamic constraints, configuration, permissions, motors and wall layout are unchanged. Player move intent is zero; physical collisions may push the dynamic player.

Precise trials invoke the existing World.FixedUpdate in paused Play. The original unique Physics2D.Simulate integrates real physics; game APIs submit actual marking requests, without injecting force, contacts or propagation.
Normal replays use actual engine FixedUpdate and onBeforeRender to submit the same game API requests. All four actions were consumed at the requested logical step.
Exactly one variable differs from E1_early in each main comparison: first target, first marking time, or an additional box recolor. Box already starts Negative, so no initial box mark is spent.
Four exploratory runs, eight confirmed repeated precise runs, four actual-engine replays and four timing-window runs, each 600 steps; 12000 successful simulated steps in total.
No damage, health, deaths, win/loss, turret or restart implementation. Player-contact counts are physical-contact samples, not proof of injury or victory.
limitations: Results reproduce on this editor/machine/settings; no cross-device determinism claim.
Early seed +/-0.2 seconds changes final recipients; guiding opportunity persists but exact color membership is timing-sensitive.
Local steering can trap actors in concave layouts; only this simple corridor tested.
No external blind playtest, physical input injection, standalone build, or proof of combat effectiveness.
Static charts show measured footprints at step 250 and sampled paths; they are not a replacement for actual engine replay evidence.
